records.problem: I want a satisfying virtual Pop-It I can click or tap, with optional sound and haptics, that stores nothing and needs no app install.
userFailures: Rapid taps register twice on one bubble because press and release both popped it.
Sound plays on every pop with no mute, which is unusable in an open office.
A 'reset all' control is missing so a finished board cannot be reused without reloading.
Haptics fire on desktop where there is no vibrator and the API rejection breaks the animation loop.

records.problem: I want a physics-based fidget spinner in the browser I can flick with mouse or touch, with momentum that feels right and optional tick sounds.
solutionWeaknesses: physics feels floaty or stops abruptly
userFailures: A flick on trackpad imparts almost no angular velocity because the tool only listened to mouse drag distance, not velocity.
The spinner never quite stops and drains battery on a phone with the tab backgrounded.
Reduced-motion users get a full spinning animation with no static alternative.
Sound ticks desync from the visual rotation after a long spin.

records.problem: I want a board of mechanical toggle switches and buttons I can flip for the tactile feedback, with optional click sounds and vibration.
solutionWeaknesses: apps bury the board behind IAP skins
no way to disable sound independently of haptics
userFailures: A toggle animates but the latch state flips back because the press handler ran twice.
Haptics and sound cannot be controlled separately, so muting also kills vibration.
Keyboard focus lands on every switch and Tab order makes the board unusable for keyboard users.
A 'all off' action is missing after exploring, so resetting means flipping dozens by hand.

records.problem: I want a simple kinetic-sand or squish surface in the browser I can drag through, without installing a game and without accounts.
solutionWeaknesses: demos are GPU-heavy on low-end phones
userFailures: Particle count is fixed so a budget phone drops to unusable frame rates with no quality preset.
Touch multitouch pinches zoom the page instead of grabbing sand because gestures were not captured.
There is no clear action and the surface packs into a corner with no reset.
Color-only depth cues make piled sand unreadable for low-vision users.

records.problem: I want a breathing-circle guide with configurable inhale/hold/exhale timings, gentle motion, and optional soft cues, fully client-side.
solutionWeaknesses: videos cannot change the timing pattern
hard to use silently without visual-only mode
userFailures: Default timings are labeled 'calm' but run faster than the user's preferred box pattern with no preset names.
Audio cue cannot be disabled independently, so a silent office session is impossible.
Reduced-motion preference is ignored and the expanding circle is the only progress signal.
Session ends with no gentle fade and an abrupt stop breaks the rhythm.

records.problem: I want a stretchy virtual slime I can poke and pull in the browser for a short sensory break, with no download.
solutionWeaknesses: apps full of IAP goo skins
no shared motion settings with other fidgets
userFailures: Slime sticks permanently to a finger event that never received pointerup after leaving the canvas.
Physics stiffness is a single magic number with no calm vs stretchy presets.
Color contrast between slime and background fails WCAG and the blob disappears on a light theme.
Performance collapses when the mesh resolution stays maxed on a low-end device.

records.problem: I want a set of intermeshing gears I can spin, with ratio labels and satisfying motion, as a fidget and a light teaching toy.
userFailures: Two gears overlap without meshing because tooth count and radius were allowed to disagree.
Direction of driven gears is wrong after adding a third idler and the label still shows the old ratio.
Dragging a gear off-canvas loses it with no undo or reset layout.
Reduced-motion users still get continuous spinning with no stepped advance control.
